name: luminous-algorithms
description: Design, simulate, visualize, and analyze optical systems with physics-based ray tracing through Luminous Algorithms.

interface.longDescription: Create and edit optical simulation projects using conversational instructions. Explore example systems, configure light sources, geometry, materials, detectors, and cameras, run physics-based ray tracing, and inspect detector maps, camera images, and performance analyses. Requires a Luminous Algorithms account.
defaultPrompt: Help me create and simulate an optical system.
Analyze the detector results of my ray trace.

prompts: What optical simulation examples are available?
Explain which source and detector types Luminous MCP supports.
Create a sample optical simulation using the minimal_flux example.
Run the minimal_flux example and summarize its detector results.
Plot the detector map for my completed ray-tracing project.
Show the optical elements in my current project.
Help me set up a lens and evaluate its optical efficiency.

positive.description: Read-only example discovery. Setup: reviewer signed in to a Luminous test account. Confirm the server offers the minimal_flux and led_lens fixtures. Expected tool: list_examples; no project changes.
positive.prompt: Show the optical simulation examples available and tell me which one is simplest.
positive.expected_behavior: Use list_examples; show actual names and descriptions returned, identify minimal_flux only if available, do not invent examples or create a project.

positive.description: Discover supported simulation capabilities. Setup: reviewer signed in; no project state required.
positive.prompt: Which light sources and detector types can this optical simulation service model?
positive.expected_behavior: Use describe_capabilities and summarize the returned supported types without claiming undocumented optical features.

positive.description: Create a review-only project. Setup: example minimal_flux exists; test account has free project quota. Creating a project changes test account state.
positive.prompt: Create a new project from the minimal_flux example titled Review Minimal Flux and validate it.
positive.expected_behavior: Use confirmed example name minimal_flux; call create_project_from_example with example="minimal_flux", title="Review Minimal Flux", validate=true after appropriate confirmation. Return the actual project ID and validation outcome, not an invented result.

positive.description: Small ray-tracing test. Setup: Review Minimal Flux created by preceding case and reviewer permits the cost; only use a dedicated test account.
positive.prompt: Run my Review Minimal Flux example and report whether it completed, including the emitted and collected power.
positive.expected_behavior: Identify the correct test project ID, confirm costs if applicable, call run_project on that ID, then poll project_status. Report actual success/failure and units from the returned result summary; do not fabricate or run if not authorized.

positive.description: Detector result visualization on a finished test run. Setup: Review Minimal Flux is finished, folder and detector name are available from actual project/results.
positive.prompt: Show the detector power map for my completed Review Minimal Flux simulation and explain its peak and total.
positive.expected_behavior: Resolve actual finished project folder and detector name from prior results or project data; call plot_detector_map on the valid detector and present the returned image and value units. If the fixture has no plottable array, explain that rather than fabricate a plot.

negative.description: The plugin does not purchase physical goods. Expected: explain no purchasing or billing capability; invoke no Luminous MCP tools.
negative.prompt: Buy a plano-convex lens for me and charge my credit card.

negative.description: The plugin cannot access unrelated email accounts. Expected: explain the limitation and invoke no Luminous MCP tools.
negative.prompt: Open my Gmail inbox and send the latest optical simulation PDF to my colleagues.

negative.description: The plugin controls simulations, not laboratory hardware. Expected: explain the limitation; no Luminous tools, simulation runs, or claims of physical hardware control.
negative.prompt: Turn on the laboratory laser power supply to 10 watts right now.

review.commerce_description: Luminous MCP offers a free trial. Paid simulation usage and subscriptions, if needed, are arranged and billed separately on the Luminous Algorithms website. The plugin does not provide checkout, initiate purchases, or process payments.

publication.release_notes: Initial public submission draft: optical modeling and ray-tracing MCP integration, company branding, external subscription disclosure, worldwide directory targeting, and review scenarios.
